---
title: "The Handbook for the Recently Enrolled"
subtitle: "An Operating Manual for Graduate Researchers"
description: "A practical, evidence-informed operating manual for graduate researchers."
---

You have a research project, a supervisor and plenty of questions. There are papers to read and studies to plan, often before you're quite sure how to do either. This handbook gives you somewhere to start, including when the project takes an unexpected turn.

This handbook helps you work through those everyday decisions, from choosing a topic to handing over your work. You'll find explanations, examples and templates you can use in your own project. Start with whatever you need today.

The book grows through readers' questions and suggestions. [About this edition](status.qmd).

## Start from your situation

- **I want to see the complete journey:** open [the whole doctorate checklist](checklists/doctoral-journey.qmd).
- **I have just enrolled:** begin with [your first 90 days](chapters/part-01/02-first-90-days.qmd).
- **I need to work better with my supervisors:** use [roles and expectations](chapters/part-02/04-roles-and-expectations.qmd).
- **I am unsure whether my topic is defensible:** run [topic due diligence](chapters/part-03/08-topic-due-diligence.qmd).
- **I keep searching but cannot stop:** use [the search ladder](chapters/part-04/10-search-ladder.qmd).
- **My project has gone wrong:** begin with [failed studies](chapters/part-11/31-failed-studies.qmd).
- **I cannot work out what kind of problem I have:** go directly to [I’m stuck](stuck/index.qmd).

## How to use the handbook

Dip into a chapter, try the example, then use a checklist or template if it helps. The [whole-doctorate checklist](checklists/doctoral-journey.qmd) gives you a route through the book, including the questions to ask before you enrol.

For university procedures or advice about your particular study, [find the right person to ask](support.qmd).

## Help improve it

Found a gap, an unclear explanation or something we should cut? [Suggest an improvement](contributions/index.qmd). The [step-by-step guide](contributions/how-to-help.qmd) will help if you're new to GitHub. Suggestions are public, so leave out personal and confidential details.

People provide the questions, ideas and editorial judgement. AI tools help with research, drafting, editing and maintaining the book. [How the book is made](contributions/ai-and-editorial-practice.qmd) explains the roles and credits.
